items.caption: A Shang oracle-script-style redraw of 大 has a tall central stroke, two diagonal strokes across it, and two strokes that diverge below. It illustrates the broad human-figure interpretation, though the figure’s pose remains disputed.
items.alt: Black glyph with a tall central stroke, two diagonal cross-strokes, and two diverging lower strokes on white.
items.selection_reason: This early script-style form makes the whole graph’s human-like outline easy to compare with the modern character; it does not settle how the figure’s pose should be interpreted.
items.period: Shang oracle-bone script style; the redraw is not a securely dated specimen.

items.caption: A Shuowen seal-script-style redraw of 大 has a central vertical stroke, broad diagonal strokes extending to either side, and two long strokes that diverge below. It provides a later script-style comparison, but not a record of the precise steps between forms.
items.alt: Black seal-style glyph with a central vertical stroke, wide diagonal strokes to either side, and two diverging lower strokes on white.
items.selection_reason: The comparison helps show broad continuity in the graph’s outline across script styles; it does not establish particular stroke changes or a chronological sequence between the redraws.

limitations.text: These are modern redrawings in named script styles, not photographs of dated artifacts. Scholarly accounts agree on a human-figure interpretation but differ over the pose; the forms alone do not establish the figure’s original meaning.

The redraws support broad comparison, but do not establish specific graphic changes or date the earliest uses of 大. The proposed development from “adult” to “big” lacks a documented dated sequence of intermediate uses.
